summary: Executed the exact-key versus brute-force-closure control on a disposable 11-entity fixture containing a three-hop cross-tenant link chain, one alias actor, one composing merge row, four households, and one account. Exact-key hashing produced 11 distinct tokens and did not unify the chain; closure produced 6 classes and put all five expected person keys into one class. Five keys diverged, including the alias actor and the external account handle. The exact-key prediction was therefore supported: per-key hashing alone violates the cross-file transitive-identity requirement. The control also showed that external account handles need an explicit alias edge to an account reference, not merely exact-string hashing. Evidence strength is one controlled fixture-level result; a full corpus and the official verifier were not run. Generalized recipe: build a small linked fixture, emit exact-key tokens and independently union all explicit edges, then compare pairwise partitions rather than only spot equality.
next_hint: The control supports a global component mechanism. The next question is the minimal normalized edge set and streaming layout that can process the full corpus within the memory cap.
